full_judgment: 10. P.W. 12 Bhanu Bibi neither in the trial court one in the enquiring court stated that she saw any of the accused appellants participating in the assault and murder of deceased Mohor Ali in any manner. She stated that she was detained at Bancharampur Police Station for two days, that the Police threatened her and that she was tutored by the Police to make a statement before the Magistrate against her will. In the committing court she stated that Police threatened her that if she did not make statement before the Magistrate as tutored by them, she and her husband would be put in danger and would be made accused in this case. She thus explains that under these circumstances to save herself and her husband she had to make an untrue statement before a Magistrate under section 164 Cr.P.C. The prosecution examined P.W. 13 Mr. M. B. Zaman, Magistrate 1st Class, Brahmanbaria who filed the statement Ext. 3 of P.W. 12 Bhanu Bibi recorded by him under section 164 Cr.P.C. on 10.11.75. Her deposition in the trial court as well as in the enquiring court is of no assistance to the prosecution. Her statement Ext. 3 recorded under section 164 Cr. P.C. cannot be treated as substantive evidence of the facts stated therein. This view finds support in the decision of Privy Council in the case of Mamand and others Vs. The King-Emperor 50 C.W.N. (P.C.) 353. Section 80 of the Evidence Act dispenses with the necessity of the formal proof of statement recorded by a competent Magistrate under section 164 Cr.P.C. as there is a presumption that such statement was genuinely recorded by the Magistrate. Such statement recorded by a competent Magistrate under section 164 Cr.P.C. can only be used for contradicting him under sections, 145 and 155 of the Evidence Act or for the purpose of corroborating him under section 157 Cr. P.C. In support of this view reference may be made to the decision in the case of Manik Gazi Vs. Emperor, A.I.R. 1942 Calcutta 36. As approver's evidence however should be corroborated by other materials and cannot be corroborated by his previous confessional statement recorded under section 164 Cr. P.C. for an approver who is an accomplice cannot corroborate himself as tainted evidence does not lose its taint by repetition. Where a witness does not substantially support his statement made under 'section 164 Cr. P.C,, his evidence must be entirely ignored (50 C.W.N. 353 Privy Council).
